title: Advanced Selectors and Combinators
description: Deep dive into advanced CSS selectors and combinators for precise element targeting.

quiz.question: Which selector selects all elements with a specific class?
quiz.explanation: The dot (.) selector targets elements by their class attribute.

quiz.question: What does the '>' combinator select?
quiz.explanation: The child combinator (>) selects immediate child elements.

quiz.question: Which selector selects the next sibling of an element?
quiz.explanation: The adjacent sibling combinator (+) selects the next sibling.

quiz.question: How do you select all siblings after an element?
quiz.explanation: The general sibling combinator (~) selects all siblings after the specified element.

quiz.question: Which pseudo-class selects the first child of its parent?
quiz.explanation: The :first-child pseudo-class targets the first child element.

quiz.question: What does the ':not()' selector do?
options: Selects elements not matching the selector inside parentheses
Selects elements matching the selector inside parentheses
quiz.correctAnswer: Selects elements not matching the selector inside parentheses
quiz.explanation: :not() excludes elements that match the selector inside it.

quiz.question: Which attribute selector matches elements with an attribute value exactly equal to a given value?
quiz.explanation: This attribute selector matches elements with attribute exactly equal to the value.

quiz.question: Which selector matches elements whose attribute value starts with a given string?
quiz.explanation: The ^= attribute selector matches attribute values that begin with the specified string.

quiz.question: What does the universal selector '*' select?
quiz.explanation: The universal selector matches every element in the document.
